jobs.occupation: Senior Project Manager within Process Automation at Novo Nordisk Engineering
jobs.description:
Does the idea of being part of the largest pharmaceutical projects in Denmark and managing complex Process Automation projects excite you? And do you thrive on defining and executing project strategies in close corporation with highly skilled colleagues? Then you’ll fit right in!

**Who We Are

**We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

**About The Role

**As a Senior Project Manager within Process Automation, you will be part of our large project portfolio in Kalundborg. You will play an important role in ensuring the successful execution of our deliveries and will be in close contact with both internal and external stakeholders.

As part of your role, you will maintain close dialogue with your team on-site and participate in regular meetings across disciplines, ensuring transparency, efficiency, and execution according to our plans.

The technical focus of this position is Process Automation, working with DCS 800xA and ECS solutions interfacing with new technologies within the Industry 4.0 domain and Manufacturing IT solutions. Our projects cover the entire project lifecycle, from conceptual and basic design phases to on-site testing activities, including FAT, Interface Testing, Wet Testing, SAT, and UAT, culminating in handover to our customers.

Based on your skills and experience, several opportunities are available within our portfolio.

Location Denmark - Kalundborg

Experience Minimum 5 Years

Department AIT Project Management

**How You Might Spend Your Days

**As a Project Manager, you will be responsible for:

• Executing projects within your area in close collaboration with your team, identifying risks and implementing mitigation measures.

• Focusing on overall project planning, ensuring delivery quality, and planning the necessary resources to maintain schedule and cost targets.

• Estimating costs and planning budgets in collaboration with our engineers and specialists.

• Managing project scope and ensuring that changes are analysed and agreed upon with stakeholders.

**Who You Are

**We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you:

• Work across the boundaries and you like to work in a diverse and international environment

• Create results through efficient project management and communication, leveraging from your relations to your team and stakeholder

• Have a personal commitment, known for your effectiveness and an open management style and know the impotency to win as a team

• Are fluent in English both written and spoken

**What You Bring To The Role

**To be successful in this role, we expect you to have the following experience and educational background:

• An educational background at bachelor's level or a similar relevant technical background.

• 6–10 years of experience with a proven track record in DCS and ECS/PLC Process Automation projects, preferably within the pharmaceutical industry.

• Experience with GMP project execution and preferable knowledge with S88 and S95

• Experience in executing Process Automation projects in collaboration with other disciplines, such as mechanical and process design, as well as end users.

• Experience with on-site commissioning activities, including FAT, SAT, and UAT.

• Project Management certification, e.g. PMP or PRINCE2, is preferred.

If you do not meet all the requirements, you are still welcome to apply and provide alternative experience that you believe would be valuable in this role.

Life at NNE NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, it means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer **here .

****Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

****Deadline of application is 15th November 2026

**Questions before applying? Send us a quick text to arrange a convenient time to chat. Contact Manager Søren Frisenborg Marker on +45 3191 8696

**Please note:

**

• We only accept applications submitted through our online recruitment system

• You do not need to attach a cover letter, but please include a few sentences about why you are applying in your resume or CV

• We invite to interviews on a running basis.

**Fair hiring:

**At NNE, we are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all job applicants. To maintain fairness, we request that you refrain from including a personal photo in your CV.

Job Description Summary

The Production Engineer – Calibration & Maintenance is responsible for the calibration, maintenance, and lifecycle management of production, inspection, measurement, and test equipment used in a regulated medical device manufacturing environment.

The role works closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, equipment owners, and external service providers to ensure equipment remains calibrated, maintained, compliant, and available for production.

Responsibilities include day-to-day calibration and preventive maintenance coordination, HxGN EAM administration, calibration assessments, controlled procedures and work instructions, supplier coordination, and equipment compliance.

This is a hands-on Production Engineering role supporting manufacturing operations across scanner/system assembly, mechanical and electrical/electronic assembly, software configuration/loading, packaging and labeling, and testing/final acceptance.

Job Description

Roles & Responsibilities

• Coordinate the site calibration program, including calibration schedules, call-in activities, equipment status, due dates, and timely completion.

• Coordinate internal and external calibration activities, including equipment preparation, shipment, return, documentation review, and release back to production.

• Ensure new, returned, overdue, failed, or out-of-tolerance equipment is appropriately assessed and controlled before use.

• Act as SME for calibration and maintenance activities in HxGN EAM, maintaining asset records, calibration setups, preventive maintenance schedules, work orders, task plans, and supporting documentation.

• Perform and support calibration assessments, including equipment requirements, criticality, acceptance criteria, calibration methods, frequencies, and maintenance needs.

• Develop and maintain calibration and maintenance procedures, SOPs, and work instructions in collaboration with equipment owners, SMEs, and Quality.

• Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance activities for production and test equipment while minimizing disruption to manufacturing.

• Support investigations, risk assessments, and product-impact assessments related to overdue, failed, or out-of-tolerance equipment, and provide input to NC/INV/CAPA activities where applicable.

• Coordinate external calibration and maintenance suppliers, including quotations, service activities, documentation, and AGORA purchase orders.

• Support internal and external audits by ensuring calibration and maintenance records are complete, traceable, compliant, and audit-ready.

• Monitor calibration and maintenance performance and drive improvements in equipment compliance, availability, data quality, and execution efficiency.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, Metrology, Maintenance, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

• Experience with calibration, preventive maintenance, equipment management, or Production Engineering in a regulated manufacturing environment.

• Understanding of calibration principles, equipment control, documentation, traceability, and manufacturing process requirements.

• Experience with computerized maintenance or Enterprise Asset Management systems, preferably HxGN EAM or comparable systems.

• Experience working within controlled procedures, work instructions, and change management processes.

• Experience coordinating suppliers, service activities, quotations, and purchase orders.

• Knowledge of GMP and Quality Management System requirements within regulated manufacturing.

Desired Characteristics

• Experience within medical device manufacturing or another highly regulated manufacturing environment.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail.

• Hands-on and practical approach to supporting manufacturing equipment and production operations.

• Structured working style with strong ownership and ability to manage recurring deadlines.

• Strong collaboration skills across Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and external suppliers.

• Clear written and verbal communication skills.

• Comfortable balancing equipment compliance, production continuity, quality requirements, and operational priorities.

• Proactive and improvement-focused approach to equipment reliability and calibration/maintenance processes

jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**Overview

**The Associate Director, Trial Delivery Team Lead plays a key leadership role in overseeing Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and Clinical Trial Associates (CTAs) while supporting the broader Clinical Trial Management (CTM) organization. This individual ensures high-quality clinical trial execution by providing strategic guidance, mentorship, and operational oversight. The Line Manager is responsible for team development, resource allocation, process optimization, and ensuring alignment with organizational goals and regulatory standards. The Trial Delivery Team Lead may assume Global Trial Lead (GTL) responsibilities to address fluctuating demands.

**Roles & Responsibilities

****Leadership and Line Management:

**

• Directly manage, mentor, and develop Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and Clinical Trial Associates (CTAs), fostering professional growth.

• Conduct performance evaluations, provide feedback, and identify training and career development opportunities.

• Ensure adequate resourcing, workload distribution, and succession planning within the team.

• Facilitate cross-functional collaboration and knowledge-sharing within the clinical operations team.

• Collaborate with Global Trial Leads (GTLs) on trial activities for assigned direct reports.

• Support trial deliverables by facilitating progress, coaching, and mentoring CTMs and CTAs.

• Advise on resource needs and support overall clinical trial resource planning.

• Ensure team success through setting clear expectations, guiding performance, and leading competency development.

• Lead functional working groups; serve as process owner or Subject Matter Expert (SME) within Clinical Operations.

• Support training initiatives across Trial Operations as needed.

• Collaborate with senior leadership to define and implement best practices within the Development Operations organization.

**Process & Compliance Management

**

• Ensure team adherence to Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ICH guidelines, and regulatory requirements (FDA, EMA, etc.).

• Develop and refine Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to optimize trial efficiency and compliance.

• Support audits, inspections, and regulatory interactions by ensuring inspection readiness across clinical trials.

• Identify and drive process improvements to enhance trial execution and data quality.

• Lead cross-trial initiatives as needed, such as implementation of Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs) or new process rollouts across the program.

• Manages the execution and implementation of CTM and CTA tasks, ensuring operational success.

• Initiates and supports the development of processes within the CTM and CTA group, focusing on practical application and continuous improvement.

• Collaborates across functions to drive efficiencies and provide day-to-day guidance to the CTM and CTA groups.

**Requirements – What You Must Have

**

• Bachelor of science degree with relevant specialization; Master of science degree preferred

• Minimum requirement of 12 or more years of experience in clinical operations

• Significant experience in leading and managing complex global clinical projects/programs

• Significant experience managing/guiding internal (cross-functional) and external (CRO, regulatory authorities) teams

• Experience with operational management and budget planning

• Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role

• Global clinical program level experience required

• Experience within the field of oncology is preferred

• Minimum 2 years’ experience as Clinical Operations representative in Clinical Development Teams (CDTs) or Global Project Teams (GPTs) would be preferable

• Experience leading team members in global matrix environment, leveraging tools and technology to ensure business needs are met.

• Strategic thinking with ability to optimize organizational resources for successful program execution

• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken

**Moreover, You Meet The Following Personal Requirements

**

• Dedicated team player who enjoys leading teams and inspire trust among colleagues

• Quality mindset and able to prioritize your work in a fast paced and changing environment

• Result- and goal-oriented and committed to contributing to the overall success of Genmab

jobs.occupation: Senior Product Manager, Scientific Software — Copenhagen
jobs.description:
Senior Product Manager, Scientific Software — Copenhagen

The company

Our client is a venture-backed Copenhagen biotech that designs a new class of oral drugs. It uses its own generative AI, automated chemistry and high-throughput biology. The platform has made and tested hundreds of thousands of novel compounds, and the company has a major pharma partnership behind it. R&D is organised under a CTO across three groups: AI & Computational Drug Design, Platform Chemistry, and Screening Biology.

The role

The Senior Product Manager will own the company's internal scientific software, so every team works from the same clean, consistent data with tools that fit together.

The company creates, moves and decides on large volumes of chemistry and biology data. Today each team builds its own solutions. The company is moving to a new data platform built for its molecules and will build custom internal products on top of it.

The Product Manager is the person who sees that three teams are building three versions of the same thing and turns them into one that works for everyone. Success is measured in time saved for the scientists: the software should save more than it costs.

Responsibilities

Product ownership

• Owns the roadmap for the internal scientific software, starting with the three products above.

• Gathers and challenges requirements from computational design, chemistry and biology, and turns parallel requests into shared solutions.

• Prioritises with the leadership team: what gets built, in what order, and why.

• Makes sure the products connect to each other and to the data platform.

• Runs user testing and adoption with the scientists, and tracks the time saved.

Delivery and leadership

• Works agile, and knows where agility stops. Ships working products within months without painting the platform into a corner.

• Leads and coordinates 3–6 developers, a mix of contractors and hires. A front-end engineer may report directly.

• Helps shape the software team as it grows.

Hands-on, at the start

• Contributes to the build until the development team is in place. The stack is Python on the back end, React/Redux on the front end, and AWS serverless services.

• Judges which components fit together and which will break, including AI-assisted code.

The profile

The ideal candidate has experience from an environment where software is built and shipped, and a scientific background. Beyond that, in order of importance:

• People leadership. Has led developers or cross-functional teams, internal or contracted, and aligned stakeholders who don't report to them.

• Product management track record. Has owned a software product or platform from idea to adoption.

• Drug discovery experience. Has worked close to design, synthesis, screening or compound selection. Broader R&D software is also relevant.

• Scientific background. A chemistry or biology degree (either is fine). Knows what they don't know, and asks.

• Hands-on coding. Can build in Python and React. Judgement matters more than depth.

Mindset: curious enough to ask "what's a canonical SMILES?", pragmatic about agile, and happy to start hands-on and grow into leading a team.

Nice to have: AWS serverless, lab automation or screening data, ELN/LIMS or compound registration, startup or scale-up experience. The working language is English.

Set-up, package and process

• Reporting. To the VP of AI & Computational Drug Design, with a weekly 1:1 and short daily stand-ups.

• Location. On site in Copenhagen, enough to work alongside the chemists and biologists in the lab. There is no fixed number of days.

• Career path. Starts senior and hands-on, and grows into leading a dedicated software team.

• Package. A competitive salary, pension, a performance bonus, and participation in the company's warrant programme.

• Process. A short screening call, then an online session where the candidate presents software they have built, then on-site interviews. The target start is early 2027.

Join Pharmacosmos in a newly established function, in a role combining people leadership with direct involvement in clinical processes, compliance and continuous improvement.

Build and lead a new Clinical Administration & Compliance function

As Director, Clinical Administration & Compliance, you will report directly to the Senior Director, Head of Clinical Operations, Trine Kolding, and take on a key role combining leadership with hands-on responsibility for clinical trial administration, processes and operational GCP compliance.

With an IoT platform connecting more millions of devices, and growing - Trackunit is building the connectivity layer underneath the construction industry. Every one of those units carries a cellular radio, and every one of those radios sits inside a web of standards, type approvals, and patent licences that decides whether we can ship and where we can ship.

You will join our IoT Division, Device Reliability Engineering (DRE) team as an expert on IoT certifications, standards, and licensing including Standard Essential Patents (SEP). This position shapes both our exposure and our coverage arguments, and it means this role works in every direction at once, with suppliers, regulatory approvals, legal advisors, product and engineering, and with customers.

This is a role for someone who can hold a genuinely complex domain in their head and then explain it in three sentences to a customer who has never heard the phrase “patent exhaustion.”

Experience level: a deep specialist role. We expect solid, hands-on experience with cellular device approvals and licensing — likely 10+ years across regulatory, certification, or IP/licensing work in mobile, IoT, or telecom hardware. This is a senior individual contributor position with no direct reports, high autonomy, and direct executive visibility.

With locations in the heart of Copenhagen, Kolding, Aarhus, and Aalborg, we offer a flexible setup with the possibility to work from one of our locations — or remotely from anywhere in Denmark.

****What's in it for you?

• A domain you will own, not administer. IoT Cellular License, SEP and certification strategy is an executive-level topic at Trackunit right now, with real financial exposure attached. You will not be filing paperwork in a corner, you will be shaping the position the company takes.

• International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders.

• We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and we support them through training, coaching, and mindfulness as well as with an open feedback culture to enable you to identify your strengths and opportunities.

• Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us or something we state in a job posting. We offer a flexible setup because we believe you know best how to structure your work. Once you have chosen how you work best, let us know what you need: we got you covered with the IT equipment you need for your work.

• Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. And this priority starts with our hiring — we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We only assess candidates on their qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and other DE&I initiatives here.

****What you'll do

****Your work splits roughly into four parts: licensing, approvals, guidance, and governance.

• Own our SEP position. Understand where our cellular SEP exposure actually sits across our device portfolio, track the relevant patent pools and licensing programmes, and maintain a clear, evidence-based view of what is covered through our supply chain and what is not.

• Run supplier licensing due diligence. Establish and maintain a consistent set of asks across module suppliers — coverage confirmation, standards and generations covered, and honest disclosure of known gaps — so responses can be compared side by side and fed into supplier qualification.

• Support licensing negotiations and claims. Work alongside our General Counsel, external patent counsel, and economic advisors on royalty basis questions, valuation and apportionment arguments, and claims that reach us through our OEM customers. You bring the technical and supply chain substance; they bring the legal strategy.

• Own global type approvals and certification. Plan and steer RED/CE, FCC, ISED, UKCA, and the wider set of regional approvals, plus GCF/PTCRB and carrier certification, across a multi-region device portfolio. Keep certification on the critical path of new product programmes rather than at the end of them.

• Stay ahead of regulatory change. Cyber Resilience Act, RED delegated acts, radio spectrum and network sunsets, environmental and product compliance requirements — know what is coming, when it bites, and what it means for our roadmap.

• Make the complex simple, and guide without over-promising. Write and maintain the internal playbooks, customer-facing explainers, and OEM guidance that turn this domain into something a commercial colleague or a customer can act on. Be the person Sales, Legal, and customers come to when a licensing notification lands, explaining the landscape accurately, saying clearly where the limits of our position are, and pointing customers to independent specialist advice where that is the right answer.

• Build the governance. Response protocols, decision records, escalation paths, and embedding licensing and compliance requirements into how we qualify suppliers and run the product development lifecycle.

****Who you are

****We think you'll need

• Strong working knowledge of cellular connectivity (e.g. LTE-M, NB-IoT, LTE Cat-1/1bis, 5G) and the direction of travel, plus a real understanding of the module and chipset landscape.

• Solid, practical experience with licensing and Standard Essential Patents in mobile or IoT devices: FRAND principles, patent pools, patent exhaustion and the limits of sublicensing, and how royalties are actually structured and argued.

• Hands-on experience with global type approvals and regulatory certification for radio products — RED/CE, FCC, and the regional approvals that come with selling hardware worldwide.

• Experience working across a hardware supply chain with module suppliers, test houses, notified bodies, and certification partners.

• Communication as a core skill, not a bonus. You can take a genuinely complicated subject and land it in plain language, in writing, with an audience that has no background in it.

• The judgement to know what we can and cannot say to a customer, and the discipline to hold that line even when it would be easier not to.

**What Matters More Than The Checklist

**

• You are honest about uncertainty. In this domain, no one can offer a blanket guarantee, and the people who claim otherwise create problems later. We would rather be accurate than reassuring.

• You are curious and self-driven, this is a field that changes constantly, and nobody is going to hand you a reading list.

• You finish things. A clear one-page answer delivered this week beats a perfect analysis that arrives after the decision was made.

• You are comfortable being the only person in the room who knows a subject, and you use that position to make others smarter rather than to make yourself indispensable.

On AI: experience with AI tooling is not a requirement, but a strong motivation and interest in working with it is. We already use AI in our daily engineering work, including MCP servers and agents against our own platform, and we see clear potential in applying it to research, documentation, and compliance workflows. We don't expect you to have experience with this but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're excited about this role and your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

****How you'll grow here

****This is a specialist role with an unusually wide view of the business, and we've set it up that way on purpose.

• Executive proximity. You will work closely with the SVP of IoT Division, while reporting into a central function for IoT, as the Device Reliability Engineering. You will help in presenting to executive leadership on exposure, risk, and recommendations. Your analysis will inform on a product technical matter (Not Legal) but with real financial and commercial decisions.

• Cross-functional reach. Legal, Finance, Product Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Sales all depend on this domain. Few roles at Trackunit touch as many parts of the company.

• External network. You will work with external patent counsel, economic consultants, module suppliers, certification bodies, and industry forums — building a network that extends well beyond Trackunit.

• Room to define the function. This discipline is being built out now. What it becomes — and whether it grows into a team — is substantially yours to shape.

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We're committed to construction one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products — it's a way of life at Trackunit. We're proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

The question is: Are you in?

**Your impact begins here

**Build and improve the applications that support colleagues across Novo Nordisk’s SAP Supply Chain area. You will work across the full stack, from user interfaces and APIs to cloud deployment and production support, in a team that values reliable software and practical engineering.

**What You’ll Bring

**We are looking for a well-rounded developer who enjoys working across frontend, backend, cloud and delivery practices. You bring:

• 2+ years of relevant software development experience, with hands-on TypeScript experience across frontend and backend development.

• Experience building cloud applications, services or APIs, and an interest in developing your skills on SAP BTP.

• Practical experience with Git, CI/CD and DevOps ways of working, including automated testing and code review.

• An ability to investigate problems, write maintainable code and work collaboratively with people in different roles.

• Strong communication skills and an interest in understanding business processes, so you can clarify needs with stakeholders and translate them into practical technical solutions.

• A compliance mindset: you understand why changes, tests, access and releases need to be controlled and traceable.

• An interest in using AI tools in your daily development work to support coding, testing and problem-solving, while applying critical judgement and taking responsibility for the quality of your work.

• Strong written and spoken English.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**Experience with SAP BTP, Node.js, SAP Cloud Application Programming Model, SAPUI5/Fiori, GitHub or enterprise integrations would be useful. GxP experience is an advantage, but it is not required; we will support you in learning the applicable processes and standards.

**What You’ll Do

**You will help develop and operate applications on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP). Working with product owners, engineers, architects and business specialists, you will turn needs into secure, maintainable solutions. You will contribute hands-on across the software lifecycle and grow your knowledge of our platforms and business processes along the way.

**Day To Day, You Will

**

• Build and maintain full-stack applications using TypeScript, including user interfaces, backend services and APIs.

• Design, test and troubleshoot cloud applications and integrations across our enterprise landscape.

• Use Git, code reviews and pipelines to build, test and release changes reliably.

• Support applications in production by investigating issues, using logs and monitoring, and improving the services you work on.

• Write clear technical documentation and apply appropriate testing, security and release controls.

• Work with teammates and stakeholders to improve existing applications, reduce technical debt and share useful engineering practices.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join SAP Quality Solutions within SAP & Ecosystems in Enterprise IT. We support Manufacturing Quality and Supply Chain processes through enterprise platforms, integrations and a portfolio of BTP applications. Product ownership, architecture, engineering and system management work closely together, giving you the opportunity to understand both the technology and the people who rely on it.

**What You Can Expect Here

**The applications you build and support help colleagues across Novo Nordisk do their work. You will have room to develop your technical skills, learn the business context and contribute ideas for making our services more reliable and easier to use. We value curiosity, sound judgement, collaboration and a willingness to learn.

**What We Offer

**At Novo Nordisk, you'll join a global healthcare company with a distinct culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

**Start now

**WHY WORK AT JOE & THE JUICE

**JOE & THE JUICE is a people-centric food and beverage company built around culture, offering much more than just juice, sandwiches, and coffee.

We believe in four simple virtues that shape everything we do:

• Positive Attitude

• Inclusion

• Social Ties

• Growth

For us, this means that when you choose a cup-half-full mindset, welcome people from every background, build real friendships across the bar by creating great guest experiences, and use every shift as a chance to learn something new, you become more than just a Juicer; like us, you continue to search and find purpose and meaning in what you do.

From your first day, you'll be part of an international network of Juicers who support each other, celebrate wins together, and push each other to grow. You will learn by doing and move through our Moneyball career path, our internal system that tracks your performance and fast-tracks you toward promotion. Most of our leaders have earned their stripes behind the bar (fun fact: over 75% of our employees started as Juicers!), so you will always be part of a company built on that same journey. If you love a fast-paced environment, music, and people, and you like the idea of turning a job into a lifestyle, JOE can become a place to build skills, friendships, and a career that takes you across cities, countries, and roles.

**JOB SUMMARY

****Full-time

****Maternity leave cover: January - June 2027

**As Senior Product Development Manager, you'll be the senior product voice in the Menu & Innovation team, owning our highest priority global NPD projects and the systems, standards and ways of working that sit behind every product we launch. Based at our Global HQ in Copenhagen, you'll work closely with Brand, Marketing, Operations, Technical, Franchise partners, Supply Chain and our supplier partners to make sure JOE products are consistently great in every market. This is a lead role in the menu & product team: you'll set the direction for how we develop, test and approve products worldwide, coach the wider team, and help shape how the team grows and operates globally. You'll have real scope to define the future of our global menu, always keeping juicer ease at the heart.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

**

• Drive end-to-end ownership of high priority global NPD projects, including new categories, new occasions and growth platforms, from brief through to in-store launch.

• Lead on all global NPD systems and processes, defining and continuously optimising them as JOE scales.

• Define and own the JOE global product testing framework and approach for all products, from scale-up kitchen trials to product operational testing to global scale commercial consumer testing.

• Lead on future NPD team growth strategies and the expansion of our global operating model.

• Own all core EPD quality workstreams across defined products and categories.

• Own all product and ingredient standards, making sure the JOE quality bar is upheld globally.

• Lead high functioning cross-functional project teams; with all global teams and local markets, from Operations and Marketing to Franchise and Supply Chain.

• Champion best-in-class trend diagnosis, coaching the wider team on how to diagnosis, read & interpret trends, in a Joe way, and run sharp competitor reviews to keep a finger on the pulse.

• Partner with all key suppliers, owning strong relationship management and engagement across current and new suppliers for current and future projects.

• Maintain and nurture a tightly connected global product network across equity and franchise; now and as it scales, so opportunities are identified, shared and recognised and everyone stays aligned.

• Key point of contact for our franchise team (current and new) on all product activity beyond equity stores; ensuring global brand consistency whilst driving local relevancy

**WHO YOU ARE

**

• A defining ability to translate concepts into scalable, operationally sound recipes without losing sight of brand and quality standards.

• Excellent project management skills and experience

• Senior stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence across functions, markets and franchise partners.

• Experience coaching and developing others

**WHAT YOU'LL BRING

**

• Min. 8 years' experience in corporate product development, ideally within QSR (Quick Service Restaurant), with a track record of owning global or multi-market launches.

• Proven experience building or improving NPD systems, processes and testing frameworks, including scale-up, operational and consumer testing.

• Deep familiarity with stage-gate or gate approval governance.

• Strong supplier management skills, with experience owning relationships across a global supply base.

• Fluent in English - other languages are a bonus!

**OUR BENEFITS

**We offer a benefits package that includes a paid pension plan, health insurance, parental leave, and additional vacation. Besides that, we provide some JOE-ified benefits:

• Our global headquarters is conveniently located in the heart of beautiful Copenhagen, where over 130 friendly faces come together!

• Enjoy our fantastic office facilities, including a fully staffed JOE & THE JUICE bar, where we serve delicious breakfast, daily lunch, refreshing juices, and top-notch barista coffee.

• At JOE, we embrace a flat hierarchy that values every opinion, creating a welcoming space for your ideas and suggestions to thrive.

• Join us for our lively monthly social calendar filled with fun activities like running club, wine tasting, creative evenings, and Friday bars-there's always something exciting happening!

• As part of our team, you'll have the opportunity to take on a BTC (Behind the Counter) shift in one of our bars twice a year, adding a unique touch to your experience.

• Stay fit and healthy with our well-equipped fitness facilities, complete with showers and a relaxing steam room to refresh after your workouts.

Ready to turn a job into a lifestyle?

**ABOUT JOE & THE JUICE

**Founded in Copenhagen in 2002, JOE & THE JUICE has grown into a global fast-casual concept with more than 500 locations across 25+ countries and over 7,000 employees worldwide, with our sights set on 1,000 stores by 2028.

Our people-centric culture and sustainability agenda are part of our Nordic heritage, and remain central to our commitment to a better future. Along the way, internal workshops and mentorship sharpen your skills, while exchange programs and international assignments can take you across our markets.

Ready to embark on this exciting journey? Apply today and become a part of JOE & THE JUICE!

We are looking for a CRM & Lifecycle Manager to join Hårklinikken as we continue to develop and grow our global ecommerce business.

We operate six Shopify sites across the US, UK, EU, Denmark, Iceland and the UAE, with the US representing our largest growth market and subscriptions playing a central role in our model.

You will own the CRM and lifecycle journey across our markets, building the communication, flows and experiences that help turn first-time clients into long-term relationships. From onboarding and treatment support to subscriptions, repeat purchase, loyalty and win-back, you will help clients stay engaged, consistent and cared for throughout their journey with us.

Working hands-on in Klaviyo and Recharge, you will use data and customer insights to understand where clients engage, where they drop off and what helps them stay. You will continuously test and improve the lifecycle journey, with a particular focus on the first 90 days and subscription retention.

Success in this role means improving 90-day retention, increasing the number of subscribers who stay for at least three deliveries, strengthening repeat purchase rates and growing CRM revenue across markets.

You will track cohorts and LTV by market and share what you learn, helping those insights shape our wider acquisition and ecommerce activities.

Primary Relationships

You will report to the Global Director of Ecommerce and work closely with the Senior Ecommerce Manager as part of our ecommerce team in Copenhagen.

You will also collaborate closely with Brand, our clinics and our Client Care Teams, particularly around campaigns, the client journey, loyalty and client feedback.

You will work closely with our Content Marketing Manager, providing clear briefs for CRM campaigns and customer communications.

Key Responsibilities

• Klaviyo. Build and run flows, segments, campaigns and SMS across six markets, working with our Content Marketing Manager who develops copy from your briefs.

• The first 90 days. Own the onboarding journey for new clients, helping them start their treatment right and stay with it.

• Subscriptions in Recharge. Manage sign-ups, retention, churn and win-back, testing what helps subscribers stay longer.

• Consultation to treatment. Develop booking reminders and post-consultation flows that help turn consultations into lasting treatments, both in our clinics and at home.

• Loyalty, reviews and client feedback. Work closely with our Client Care Team to understand where clients get stuck and what brings them back.

• The campaign calendar. Coordinate the campaign calendar so CRM, the site and paid media go live at the same time with the same message.

Core Competencies

This role requires strong CRM and lifecycle experience combined with a hands-on, structured and analytical approach. You are comfortable working with data, understanding customer behaviour and turning insights into actions that strengthen retention.

You keep many moving parts on track and care about the client, not just the open rate. You understand how to grow retention through value rather than discounts, and you know when one email is one too many. You don't need to tick every box to be the right fit. We would love to hear from you if you bring strong CRM or lifecycle experience, a customer-focused mindset, a genuine interest in building relationships that last and supporting our mission

What You Bring:

• 3-5 years of experience in CRM, retention or lifecycle marketing, ideally within DTC ecommerce.

• Strong hands-on Klaviyo skills, with experience building flows, segments and templates yourself.

• Experience with subscriptions, ideally Recharge.

• A track record of delivering results that you can demonstrate through data.

• Confidence working with data, with the ability to read a cohort and understand what to test next.

• Fluent English.

It is an advantage if you also have:

• Experience working across several markets or Shopify storefronts, ideally including the US.

• Experience with a premium beauty, wellness or personal care brand with a regimen or subscription model.

• Experience with loyalty or review platforms.

• Proficiency in a Scandinavian language.

Who Are We?

Founded in 1992 in Copenhagen, Hårklinikken is a leading scalp and hair health clinic with more than 30 years of experience. We help clients achieve optimal scalp health and long-lasting hair gain, combining expert guidance with clean and gentle products formulated to support healthy hair growth.

Our approach began with Hårklinikken’s founder and lead researcher, Lars Skjøth, who developed a diagnostic, consultation-based approach centred around understanding each client’s individual scalp and hair needs. Today, The Hårklinikken Method brings together decades of expertise with the personalised care that has been at the heart of Hårklinikken from the beginning.

Clients come to us in different ways, whether through a consultation or by discovering and purchasing our products online. Through virtual consultations or in person at our clinics in New York, Beverly Hills, Copenhagen, Aarhus, Dubai and Reykjavik, our Hair Specialists combine their expertise with an individual assessment of each client’s scalp, hair, lifestyle and environment to create a personalised regimen designed around their specific needs.

jobs.occupation: Supply Chain Launch Manager for global launch projects
jobs.description:
Supply Chain Launch Manager for global launch projects

Would you like to help orchestrate the global launch of new products, representing our supply chain throughout the entire launch projects?

Join a global group of skilled supply chain professionals and follow new products from early development all the way to market – as your input will ensure that we deliver the best products to people with intimate healthcare needs.

“WE play a key part in planning and executing successful launches – and we are a valued voice in the process, allowing us to set a clear direction,” explains Head of Supply Chain Launch, Global Supply Chain Management, Daniel Arildsen.

Join our highly experienced Launch department

Together, we are 7 colleagues, responsible for supply chain activities related to bringing new and innovative products to market within Chronic Care and Wound Care products. A good part of our time, we spend working with our factories in Hungary, Costa Rica, and soon Portugal.

“As we are each dedicated to different projects, discussing what we’ve learned with each other is very important to us. And we’ll be there to make sure you get to ease into the position,” says Daniel.

Ensure that supply chain is covered in every project

As part of the Coloplast global supply chain, you will find yourself in the middle of a web of stakeholders working towards launching new Chronic Care and Wound Care products. Here, you will be dedicated to specific projects, acting as supply chain lead or subject matter expert, representing the voice of supply chain and making sure supply chain is on track for launch.

Specifically, you will be the subject matter expert from supply chain, staying up to date on project progression. Moreover, you will plan the launch and make sure that systems, manufacturing, stock levels, etc. are ready for launch. And when you meet a bump in the road, you will figure out solutions with the project team.

From early project development until post-launch, you will:

•    Influence project decisions and direction early, to avoid supply chain risks

•    Drive the supply chain plan with manufacturing sites, balancing project deliverables and commercial considerations to launch on time

•    Produce launch scenarios in collaboration with other departments and ensure alignment with the rest of the organization

•    Coordinate activities at our production sites and flag supply chain risks

•    Make sure systems, such as planning, base data and distribution, are ready for launch

•    Follow up on delivery performance of newly launched items after launch

Your work may take you traveling roughly 2 weeks per year, primarily to our factory in Hungary. However, you will have a say on how the trips are planned, so they will fit with the rest of your life.

Supply chain knowledge and stakeholder management skills

In this role, you must be able to work cross-functionally, using your good stakeholder management skills to incorporate a wide range of input from across the business. Also, you can work with limited supervision in your projects, representing the voice of supply chain, making decisions, and setting a direction for your area.

Finally, we imagine that you:

•    Have a degree in supply chain or engineering

•    Have some experience, either within supply chain or logistics and a good conception of production processes

•    Possibly have some experience working in projects, allowing you to consider both commercial and supply chain perspectives

•    Are good at Excel and at adapting to new systems

•    Are fluent in English

Interested?

If you would like to know more about the position, please reach out to Head of Supply Chain Launch,

Global Supply Chain Management, Daniel Arildsen on DKDAAR@coloplast.com. We will take candidates into the recruitment process continuously, so do not hesitate to apply. This position will remain open until a suitable candidate has been found.

Pursuing an ambitious growth agenda, Coloplast develops and markets products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. Employing about 16.000 people and with products available in more than 143 countries, we are one of the world´s leading medical device companies. We are constantly growing our business and always looking for new ways to move forward – we explore, learn and look for new ways of doing things.

Coloplast is committed to being an inclusive organization, where people bring their differences to work each day, fulfil their potential and have a strong sense of belonging because – and not despite – of their differences. We therefore encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender, age, race, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religious belief or physical ability.

Visit us on Coloplast.com.

Watch the film. Follow us on LinkedIn.

jobs.description:
Experienced Data Scientist for Agentic Applications - Aarhus or Gdansk

Available in 2 locations

Viby J, Denmark, 8260

Gdansk, Poland, 80-244

Category: Information Technology

Permanent

Do you want to help shape the next generation of AI-powered business capabilities and are you motivated by turning business opportunities into intelligent agentic products?

“At Arla, we are scaling proven Data Science and Machine Learning capabilities into business-critical products that support commercial decisions across our markets. We are looking for someone who can combine strong quantitative modelling skills with modern software and AI engineering practices to help drive this journey.” says Andreas Therkildsen, Manager, IT Product Architect.

How you will make an impact

You will join a dedicated product team responsible for the Net Revenue Management (NRM) Commercial Intelligence Platform and its growing portfolio of pricing, promotion, forecasting, and AI-enabled capabilities. Working closely with commercial stakeholders, product owners, architects, engineers, and data specialists, you will:

• Build a deep understanding of pricing, promotions, demand drivers, and commercial decision-making within Net Revenue Management.

• Design and develop statistical, econometric, and machine learning models that generate actionable business insights.

• Apply Machine Learning models and inference techniques to evaluate commercial initiatives and identify revenue opportunities, and understand why the models perform as they do.

• Develop and operationalize forecasting, pricing, and promotional effectiveness models in production environments.

• Partner up with engineers and architects to establish scalable MLOps, model monitoring, and AI-enabled development practices.

• Help identify and mature new AI and Data Science opportunities into trusted business capabilities that create measurable value.

What will make you successful

You have hands-on experience with Data Science, Machine Learning, Data Engineering and modern AI tooling. You enjoy solving real business challenges and working at the intersection of business, data, and technology. You understand that successful solutions require strong statistical foundations, trusted data, and robust engineering practices. The ideal candidate brings:

• Strong experience with Bayesian hierarchical models using tools such as PyMC, Stan, or NumPyro, combined with solid statistical inference and model validation practices.

• Strong econometrics and causal inference expertise, including price elasticity modelling, endogeneity challenges, and deriving reliable insights from real-world commercial data.

• Strong Python and SQL skills, combined with experience deploying and maintaining models through automated pipelines, monitoring, testing, versioning, and MLOps practices.

• Practical experience with machine learning approaches such as XGBoost, LightGBM, and forecasting techniques for demand and baseline prediction.

• Daily use of AI-enabled development tools such as Claude, Codex, GitHub Copilot, or similar, with the ability to critically evaluate generated outputs.

• A product-oriented mindset and the ability to translate business opportunities into scalable analytical solutions.

It is an advantage if you also have experience with:

• Pricing, Promotions, Revenue Growth Management, Commercial Intelligence, or Net Revenue Management.

• Optimization techniques and decision modelling using tools such as OR-Tools, Pyomo, or Gurobi.

• Advanced causal inference methods such as Causal Forests, Synthetic Control, Bayesian Structural Time Series, DoubleML, or EconML.

• Time-series forecasting approaches such as state-space models or Prophet.

• Databricks, Spark, Azure, and modern cloud-based data platforms.

• Retail and consumer datasets, or an MSc/PhD within Statistics, Econometrics, Data Science, Mathematics, or a related discipline.

What do we offer?

This position is based in Aarhus, Denmark or Gdańsk, Poland, with an expectation of 50% office presence. You will work alongside skilled product teams, architects, engineers and data specialists and can help shape the future of AI-powered commercial capabilities within one of Arla’s strategically important business domains. We offer a flexible hybrid working model, competitive salary and benefits, and opportunities for professional development in a rapidly evolving AI landscape.

Would you like to join us?

If you are ready to help turn AI opportunities into real business value, we would love to hear from you. We review applications on an ongoing basis and may close the process once the right candidate is found.

For more information, please contact Andreas Therkildsen, Manager, IT Product Architect, athec@arlafoods.com.

Shape the Future of Dairy

Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. If you are looking to shape the future with an ambitious global cooperative that truly cares about your growth, where everyone feels valued and empowered, and collaboration is the core of culture, Arla is a choice you can feel good about.

jobs.occupation: Senior Director, Commercial Excellence & Commercial Strategy
jobs.description:
Do you thrive at the intersection between commercial strategy, transformation and execution. Do you enjoy setting the direction and then rolling up your sleeves to make it happen? Join 3Shape’s CCO Leadership Team and shape how a global MedTech leader grows. We are looking for someone who isn’t afraid to challenge the status quo and brings a healthy disruptive edge to how things are done.

About 3Shape

3Shape started with a simple idea: to make 3D scanning better. We applied it first to the hearing industry and then to dentistry, and today our scanning and CAD/CAM solutions help dental and hearing professionals treat more people, more effectively. Every second of every day, a 3Shape scanner is in use somewhere in the world. We are 2,200+ colleagues of 45+ nationalities, headquartered in central Copenhagen at Kongens Nytorv.

Our commercial organisation is approximately 1,000 people strong and delivers our products to customers in 29 countries across Europe, the Americas and Asia. Our flagship products include a mixture of hardware and software; TRIOS intraoral scanners, the Dental System CAD software and the 3Shape Unite platform.

Your new role

As Senior Director, Commercial Excellence & Commercial Strategy, you report directly to our SVP of Commercial (CCO) and act as a close sparring partner. You sit on the CCO Leadership Team with the leaders of Global Customer Success, Global Marketing and our three Regional VPs, and you lead a team of Commercial Excellence Managers, transformation agents, project managers and data and reporting specialists.

You own the commercial strategy for Dental Clinics, DSOs (dental service organisations) and Laboratories, and you build Commercial Excellence into a global function that turns strategic choices into growth across markets.

Leading leaders and running Commercial Excellence should come naturally to you. The real stretch in this role is driving a transformation and professionalization of the commercial organization with the aim of lifting topline growth.

You will work side by side with colleagues at our Copenhagen headquarters in Denmark, in an office-based role, and you will regularly travel to spend time with our great people in local sales hubs and meet customers at leading dental events around the world.

What you will do

Commercial strategy & transformation

• Own the three-year commercial strategy and the annual commercial strategy cycle, linked to budget, targets and business plans.

• Turn the strategy into a roadmap with clear owners, milestones and KPIs, and keep execution on track.

• Lead the CCO transformation portfolio and challenge how we get most impact across segments, markets, channels and new offerings.

• Build alignment across global functions, regions and markets, including through our Country Manager forum.

Commercial Excellence

• Define and scale the global Commercial Excellence operating model, from customer potential and territory management to sales plays and tools.

• Turn market, customer and competitor insight into decision-ready recommendations for the CCO Leadership Team.

• Set the CRM standard and the commercial performance framework together with IT, Data Management and Financial Planning & BI.

• Partner with Finance and Portfolio and Product Strategy (PPS) on pricing and discount governance, and enable go-to-market for new offerings.

• Drive launch excellence for new products and offerings, with a repeatable launch playbook, clear market readiness criteria and adoption KPIs that get new solutions into customers’ hands quickly across all markets.

What success looks like

• A three-year commercial strategy with clear priorities agreed in the CCO Leadership Team and linked to budget and targets.

• Commercial transformation delivering tangible impact with revenue growth, efficiency gains and capability uplift in priority markets, with learnings carried into the rest.

• Commercial Excellence established as a recognised discipline, with a strong team and a clear role across Commercial, Portfolio and Product Strategy (PPS) and Finance.

• CRM adopted to standard in all markets, and leadership decisions taken on a shared, current picture of market, customers and competitors.

• A proven launch excellence model in place, with new offerings reaching target adoption faster across markets.

Who you are

You are an experienced senior commercial leader with documented results from comparable roles. You hold a master’s degree in economics, business or similar, and you bring:

• Experience leading leaders and engaging, inspiring and developing people.

• A track record of owning and driving commercial strategy from within the business, rather than as an external advisor, with measurable results to show for it.

• Deep Commercial Excellence experience, including shaping and growing the function in a fast-growing organisation. MedTech experience is a plus.

• Experience leading complex, cross-functional transformations with executive stakeholders.

• Executive presence and the courage to challenge senior leaders and established ways of working.

• International experience from a global matrix organisation.

What 3Shape offers

• Real influence on how a global MedTech leader grows, a premium brand guided by innovation and customer focus.

• A strategic mandate across regions to shape our global commercial approach, with real room to influence and make decisions.

• A seat on the CCO Leadership Team and high visibility with senior leaders across 3Shape.

• A role as the CCO’s personal sparring partner on the commercial path forward.

• Global scale and impact across 29 countries, and the opportunity to lead a strong, international team.

• An attractive healthcare package, daily breakfast and lunch from our own chefs, and plenty of social clubs and activities.

• Modern offices in central Copenhagen, near Kongens Nytorv and Nyhavn.

Application process

• To apply, click "Apply now" and attach your CV including a short motivation in one document.

• Applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

We encourage all relevant applicants to apply. We are committed to celebrating human diversity, and we trust that the best way to reach outstanding business results, is by welcoming diverse people into our community.

Operations, Full time, Copenhagen, Denmark

**About Apylon And The Opportunity

**Apylon is building the intelligent revenue management platform for European healthcare. Billions of euros flow between hospitals and insurers through fragmented, manual workflows — a maze of rules, conditions and requirements.

We believe this is a machine learning and automation problem disguised as financial operations.

Apylon is backed by experienced operators and top-tier investors in healthcare and fintech. Our team draws on experience from Zendesk, Pleo, Wawa Fertility, Sibill, and some of the largest multi-country hospital groups in Europe.

As a Founders Associate, you’ll work directly with the founding team on the highest-priority challenges facing the company. This is a unique opportunity to gain exposure to all aspects of building a venture-backed startup — from strategy and operations to customer success and fundraising.

Delivering healthcare is hard. Getting paid for it shouldn’t be.

You’ll be responsible for

• Working directly with founders on day-to-day operations, strategic initiatives and special projects.

• Supporting customer onboarding and success — ensuring our healthcare clients get maximum value from Apylon.

• Conducting market research and competitive analysis to inform product and go-to-market strategy.

• Building and improving internal processes and operations as we scale.

• Supporting fundraising efforts — preparing materials, coordinating with investors, and managing due diligence.

• Wearing many hats — from data analysis to customer calls to operational firefighting.

• Helping build the company culture and team as we grow.

Who you are

• 1-3 years of experience in consulting, investment banking, venture capital, or a high-growth startup.

• Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills — you can structure ambiguous problems and drive to solutions.

• Strong communication skills — you can write clearly and present confidently.

• Highly organized with excellent attention to detail.

• Self-starter who takes ownership and gets things done without constant direction.

• Comfortable with ambiguity and rapid change — you thrive in fast-paced environments.

• Genuinely curious about healthcare, fintech, and building companies.

Bonus points

• Previous startup experience or entrepreneurial ventures.

• Experience in healthcare or fintech.

• Fluency in German, Danish, or Italian.

• Technical background or comfort working closely with engineering teams.

What Apylon offers

• The chance to solve one of Europe’s biggest healthcare inefficiencies.

• Competitive salary + stock options (you’ll own part of what you build).

• 25 days of annual leave + local public holidays.

• Lunch on us

• Regular off-sites and social events — we like building together, not just working together.

• Unparalleled learning opportunity — direct exposure to all aspects of building a company.

• A clear path to growth as the company scales.

• This role may require international travel within the EU on a roughly monthly cadence.

Working at Apylon means embarking on a highly ambitious mission to rebuild the financial infrastructure of European healthcare. We’re already live with leading private hospitals, processing thousands of invoices, proving that complex payer rules can be turned into code - powering transparent, automated, and intelligent revenue operations.

How to apply. If you're excited by the challenge of building intelligent, high-impact systems at the core of European healthcare and enjoy shipping fast, we'd love to hear from you.

**Your Impact

**

• Identify, evaluate and develop suppliers for customised components, balancing quality, cost, delivery performance, sustainability and supply chain risk.

• Negotiate framework agreements, contracts and pricing structures that support volatile demand, complex components and project-specific requirements.

**How To Apply

**Please submit your CV via our careers page. Applications are reviewed on receipt and interviews are scheduled on a rolling basis.

**WHY WORK AT JOE & THE JUICE

**JOE & THE JUICE is a people-centric food and beverage company built around culture, offering much more than just juice, sandwiches, and coffee.

We believe in four simple virtues that shape everything we do:

• Positive Attitude

• Inclusion

• Social Ties

From your first day, you'll be part of an international network of Juicers who support each other, celebrate wins together, and push each other to grow. You will learn by doing and move through our Moneyball career path, our internal system that tracks your performance and fast-tracks you toward promotion. Most of our leaders have earned their stripes behind the bar (fun fact: over 75% of our employees started as Juicers!), so you will always be part of a company built on that same journey. If you love a fast-paced environment, music, and people, and you like the idea of turning a job into a lifestyle, JOE can become a place to build skills, friendships, and a career that takes you across cities, countries, and roles.

**JOB SUMMARY

**The AP Manager leads the Accounts Payable team and is responsible for ensuring accurate, compliant, and timely processing of supplier invoices and payments globally, safeguarding financial integrity and operational efficiency. The role ensures high-quality Accounts Payable execution across the team, oversees month-end and audit processes, and acts as the escalation point for suppliers and internal stakeholders. As part of Shared Services, reporting to the Head of P2P, this position leads a team of 7 FTEs across multiple entities and is accountable for financial governance, KPI performance, and driving the function's transition from manual to automated, scalable processes. The role is a full-time position and reports to the Head of Procure to Pay.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

**

• Lead, coach and develop a team of 7 FTEs across the Accounts Payable function.

• Approve journals and oversee approval of new vendors and vendor changes.

• Own the monthly close process for Accounts Payable, ensuring accuracy and timely delivery.

• Manage and delegate audit deliverables across quarterly, interim, and yearly cycles.

• Maintain control and oversight of the supplier invoice workflow, including monitoring and clearing backlog to keep processing on track.

• Own KPI reporting and performance tracking, providing visibility to the Head of P2P and key stakeholders.

• Drive continuous improvement, leading automation and process projects to move the function towards scalable, less manual ways of working.

• Ensure adherence to company policies, financial controls, and regulatory requirements, maintaining strong governance within the AP function.

**KEY EXPECTATIONS

**In this role, you take full ownership of your team's output and workload distribution, manage complex operational and people challenges, and drive process improvement across the function. You lead rather than execute - setting direction, removing blockers, and holding the team accountable to a high standard. You build the case for change, adapt quickly when priorities shift, and are a dependable leader who drives both team performance and function-wide results.

**OUR BENEFITS

**We offer a benefits package that includes a paid pension plan, health insurance, parental leave, and additional vacation. Besides that, we provide some JOE-ified benefits:

• Our global headquarters is conveniently located in the heart of beautiful Copenhagen, where over 200 friendly faces come together!

• Fantastic office facilities, including a fully staffed JOE & THE JUICE bar, where we serve delicious breakfast, daily lunch, refreshing juices, and top-notch barista coffee.

• At JOE, we embrace a flat hierarchy that values every opinion, creating a welcoming space for your ideas and suggestions to thrive.

• Lively monthly social calendar filled with fun activities like running club, wine tasting, creative evenings, and Friday bars - there's always something exciting happening!

• As part of our team, you'll have the opportunity to take on a BTC (Behind the Counter) shift in one of our bars twice a year, adding a unique touch to your experience.

• Ready to turn a job into a lifestyle?

**ABOUT JOE & THE JUICE

**Founded in Copenhagen in 2002, JOE & THE JUICE has grown into a global fast-casual concept with more than 500 locations across 25+ countries and over 7,000 employees worldwide, with our sights set on 1,000 stores by 2028.

Our people-centric culture and sustainability agenda are part of our Nordic heritage, and remain central to our commitment to a better future. Along the way, internal workshops and mentorship sharpen your skills, while exchange programs and international assignments can take you across our markets.

Ready to embark on this exciting journey? Apply today and become a part of JOE & THE JUICE!
